Patient: Dana Whitfield
Service: MRI Lumbar Spine without contrast
Date of Service: October 3, 2026

I am writing to formally request an internal appeal of the adverse benefit determination issued on October 19, 2026, denying coverage for the MRI lumbar spine without contrast performed on October 3, 2026. The denial stated: "The requested imaging is not medically necessary. Our records do not show that you completed at least six (6) weeks of conservative therapy before imaging was performed, as required by our Advanced Imaging Clinical Policy (CP-IMG-114)."

This denial incorrectly applies the six-week conservative therapy requirement despite clear red flag findings documented in the medical records that satisfy criterion (b) of CP-IMG-114, which explicitly exempts the conservative therapy prerequisite. According to Section 4.2 Advanced Imaging Clinical Policy (CP-IMG-114) — Lumbar Spine MRI, "MRI of the lumbar spine is considered medically necessary for low back pain when ANY of the following criteria are met: ... (b) the member presents with 'red flag' findings, including progressive or severe neurological deficit (e.g. motor weakness, foot drop, loss of reflexes)... Conservative therapy is not required when criterion (b) is met."

The clinic note from Lakeside Orthopedic & Spine dated September 29, 2026 documents: "New numbness in left foot and difficulty lifting left foot when walking, noticed 5 days ago. Exam: Left ankle dorsiflexion strength 3/5 (right 5/5). Left extensor hallucis longus 3/5. Diminished sensation over dorsum of left foot (L5 dermatome)." These findings confirm progressive motor deficit consistent with left foot drop and L5 radiculopathy, satisfying the red flag criterion. Critically, these red-flag findings were documented on September 29, 2026, and the MRI was ordered urgently that same day, performed October 3, demonstrating that imaging was indicated based on acute neurological deterioration.

Furthermore, criterion (c) of CP-IMG-114 is independently satisfied, as the September 29 clinic note includes a plan for "surgical consult depending on findings," and the October 7, 2026 spine surgery consult recommended left L4-L5 microdiscectomy, scheduled for October 21, 2026. Since conservative therapy is not required when either criterion (b) or (c) is met, the denial’s reliance on the six-week conservative therapy rule is invalid.

The MRI was medically necessary under the plan’s definition, as a prudent physician would order imaging to evaluate progressive neurological deficit suggestive of compressive pathology requiring possible surgical intervention. Section 7.3 Definition of Medical Necessity states: "Medically Necessary means health care services that a prudent physician would provide to a patient to diagnose or treat an illness or injury in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice..." The September 29, 2026 clinic note records: "Assessment: Left L5 radiculopathy with progressive motor deficit (partial foot drop). Suspect L4-L5 disc herniation. Plan: Urgent MRI lumbar spine without contrast to evaluate for compressive lesion; surgical consult depending on findings." The subsequent MRI report dated October 3, 2026 confirms: "Impression: Large left paracentral disc extrusion at L4-L5 with severe compression of the traversing left L5 nerve root. Moderate central canal stenosis," validating the clinical urgency.

Although conservative therapy was not required due to the presence of red flags, treatment had been initiated and failed, with worsening symptoms despite ibuprofen starting September 5, activity modification, and four physical therapy sessions beginning September 12. The September 29 clinic note states: "Onset after lifting boxes on September 1, 2026. Started ibuprofen 600 mg TID and activity modification at urgent care visit on September 5, 2026. Began physical therapy September 12, 2026 (4 sessions). Pain now 8/10." The physical therapy progress note dated September 26, 2026 adds: "Patient reports increased left leg pain and new tingling in left foot. Unable to complete heel walking on left. Therapist notes decline in function since initial evaluation on September 12, 2026. Recommend physician re-evaluation." This demonstrates treatment failure and disease progression, further supporting the necessity of timely imaging.

Under Section 9.2 Peer-to-Peer Review, I note that the treating provider, Dr. Priya Raman, should directly request a peer-to-peer discussion with the Plan’s medical reviewer to clarify the clinical indications, consistent with the policy’s intent. I also request a full copy of the claim file and all criteria used in the denial decision.

Based on the policy language and clinical evidence—specifically the satisfaction of criteria (b) and (c) of CP-IMG-114—I request that Northwind Health Plan overturn the denial and authorize payment for the MRI lumbar spine without contrast performed on October 3, 2026, in the amount of $2,340.00.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Dana Whitfield
